system.summary: The State Department code WE028 (about 1,600 numbers; Weber 1979) in a copy whose sixteen blocks of 100 run in reverse order (Claiborne n = WE028 100*(15-i)+r for n = 100*i+r), as in Anthony Morris's copy; I/J and U/V merged; final hook = -s, triangle = -ed. The contributor described it, before the match, as alphabetical segments of variable length in permuted order.

prior_solution.where: Jacob Wagner's interlinear decipherments, printed in PJM-SS 10:464-65, 11, 13 and Rowland, Official Letter Books of W. C. C. Claiborne 3:211-213. The key itself is listed as not found by the editors; no reconstruction found. Nothing in this repository (12 Nov 2026). Integration 14 Nov 2026: the code is WE028 with reversed blocks; WE028 is printed in Weber 1979 and its copy at NARA M97 r13 is transcribed in this repository (morris1813, 11 Nov 2026); the block reversal was found for Morris's copy here (morris1813). PJM-SS 'key not found' confirmed only from Founders search snippets.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol before the calculation). An AI agent transcribed, aligned and built the partial key; no human palaeographer checked.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Groups of the three NARA pieces transcribed line by line.
328 words aligned with the printed decipherments; 261 numbers valued (89 sure, 145 probable, 27 doubtful).
One-and-a-half-part code: alphabetical segments of variable length, permuted; 96 % of sure/probable pairs in order within pages of 50 (controls <= 57 %).
Held-out letter of 25 Nov 1806: 22 of 23 testable new groups fall at their alphabetical place.
History of the code from Founders and Rowland: sent 8 July 1805, received 12 Aug 1805; Graham's Weber 419-30 code is Sargent's, a different one.

Integration check: the three NARA images (T260 r7 0224-0226, r8 0045, 0409) fetched; the 62 groups of 25 Nov 1806 and the 99 of 13 Jan 1806 all agree with transcription.txt; about 150 groups of 24 Oct 1805 compared: two misreads (learn 135 -> 185; lakes 1482L -> 148L, the hook read as a 2), two places unsettled (arrival 1?0, leather 1?37).
Own script: order test 96.4% of 197 pairs (shuffled median 49.7%, max 56.9% in 1,000); 28 groups only in the held-out letter, 27 consistent with the page bounds of the other letters (1116 'd' not).

Contributor's key compared with every State Department key in the repository: king1797, the Pinckney/legation codes, jqa (WE028 direct), Armstrong 972, Mountflorence: no agreement. WE028 with the blocks of 100 reversed (morris1813's map): 223 of 261 values exact (S 85/89, P 125/145, D 13/27); the jqa table under the same reversal 169 of 237 against at most 63 for 1,000 random block orders.

WE028 reversed applied unchanged to the 328 aligned words (we028_check.py): 294 reproduce Wagner's word mechanically, 23 more by the clerk's spelling, overlaps, numerals or a re-split of 'General Wilkinson' and 'General binding' (fixing the doubtful 149, 232, 484); 3 encoder slips (611 order in information, 235 bil for the, John 101 51), troops 1077 tra x3, 5 unsettled on the image or alignment. Graham's 1806 code (graham1806) does not fit the reversed table.

Image 0226 (T260 roll 7, end of 24 Oct 1805) compared group by group: the 57 live groups agree with transcription.txt except the second Lakes, 153 1482L -> 153 148L (the final hook read as a 2, as on 0225; added to transcription_corrections.tsv). Before 'of' (76) the clerk wrote 362 285 (';' 'the'), then struck 153 148L 1 12 (an eye-skip to 'Lakes a few' two lines below); 'collecting' has no group: Wagner's gloss supplies it. With the correction we028_check.py gives 295 of 328 words mechanically (was 294); by hand 319 of 328 (was 317): the second Lakes and 'the' now fit, 'collecting' joins the encoder slips.

Entry 1077 = tra: in Beling's transcription both halves of the M97 r13 sheet read tra, and the block runs tol, ton, too, tor, total, toward, town, tra, trac, tract, traction (WE028 570-580), so tro cannot stand at 1077 in alphabetical order; WE028 has no tro or troop entry at all (tre 854, tri 856, tru 857 in Morris numbering). Morris uses 1077 for con-tra-ry (No. 18, 20 Sep 1814) and writes troops as 1519 (trouble, cut back by strokes) + 603 op. Claiborne's clerk wrote tro- as 1077 tra three times: a consistent substitution of the nearest syllable, not a misread of the sheet. The sheet image itself was not re-read here.

Letters of 18 and 19 Nov 1806 (Library of Congress, Burr Conspiracy Collection; NARA T260 roll 8 image 0408 is a typed slip saying they were removed there). Their clear text is in print twice: the coded words decoded in PJM-SS 13 (Founders 02-13-02-0066 and -0069) and Claiborne's letterbook copy in clear, Rowland, Official Letter Books 4:36-37 (Internet Archive officialletterbo04clai). Images: www.loc.gov and its JSON API answer scripts with a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403), so whether the collection (one microfilm reel) is digitized could not be checked; no image, no transcription, no decoding. Territorial Papers IX is not open on the Internet Archive and HathiTrust answers with the same kind of challenge: not consulted.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Integration check 14 Nov 2026: the code is the State Department code WE028 (Weber 1979; surviving copy NARA M97 roll 13 frames 1056-1057, transcribed in ../morris1813/beling/key/) with its sixteen blocks of 100 in reverse order, the same copy order as Anthony Morris's (targets/morris1813). Applied unchanged (we028_check.py), it reproduces Wagner's word for 294 of 328 aligned words by a mechanical rule and 317 of 328 after hand classification. The contributor's own partial key (adjacent plaintext: Wagner's interlinear decipherments) was built before this match, by the contributor's record, and agrees with it (85 of 89 sure values exactly, the other 4 spelling variants). The texts themselves were deciphered in 1805-1806 by Wagner.

validation.notes: Structure: 22/23 held-out groups at their place; 96 % order in pages of 50 against <= 57 % for controls. Not a validation of a complete key. Reproduced here 14 Nov 2026: 96.4% of 197 adjacent pairs, shuffled median 49.7%, max 56.9% (own script); 28 groups occur only in the held-out letter. The held-out status is by the contributor's record. The structure is now explained by WE028 with reversed blocks, which also confirms the key from outside.

outcome.fraction_read_source: The texts are Wagner's 1805-1806 decipherments (printed); not new. Key coverage, measured by we028_check.py on transcription.txt with transcription_corrections.tsv: 295 of 328 words (89.9%) reproduced mechanically by WE028 reversed, 319 of 328 (97.3%) after hand classification (NOTES, Integration check and Second pass). The contributor's own key, sure values only: 326 of 550 groups (59.3%), 202 of 328 words with every group sure (61.6%).
